For every $\epsilon >0$ there is $C'(\epsilon )<\infty $ such that every $(x,t)$ lies either in the core of a $(C',\epsilon )$-cap, at the center of an evolving $\epsilon $-neck starting at $0$ and initially disjoint from the surgery cap, or at the center of an evolving $\epsilon $-neck defined for rescaled time $1+\epsilon $.

↗ thm:standard-solution-canonical-neighborhoods ↗ prop:standard-solution-scalar-curvature-lower-bound ↗ prop:standard-flow-asymptotic-cylinder \sketch Apply the high-curvature theorem above. At bounded curvature, the scalar lower bound restricts time away from $1$; cylindrical asymptotics give the outer necks and compactness gives caps on the remaining compact set.

\label{stdsolncannbhd}

For every $\epsilon>0$ there is $C'(\epsilon)<\infty$ such that every
$(x,t)$ lies either in the core of a $(C',\epsilon)$-cap, at the center
of an evolving $\epsilon$-neck starting at $0$ and initially disjoint from
the surgery cap, or at the center of an evolving $\epsilon$-neck defined
for rescaled time $1+\epsilon$.
\end{theorem}
